comment: Paths the estate depends on. Each must be kept: tracked in a repo, mirrored in by tracked.json, or generated by something that is. Adding a line here is how a new class of file gets guarded. LAW 24.

paths.why: the laws every agent on this machine obeys
what each law cost, and why it says what it says
what every session loads at startup
the agent definitions the Agent tool resolves
the skills sessions invoke by name
what the estate has learned; injected into every session, so losing it costs every agent the same week twice (LAW 30)

repos.why: the guards, the board, the mirror
repos.public_by_ruling: founder, 2026-08-23: 'sort this out nake then public if u have 2'. Private repos on this account have every Actions job refused before its first step, so a ships-from repo is public on purpose. c_ci_reach() in estate_audit.py owns its visibility and heals it; do not add 'private' back here.

repos.why: The Architect (works on a feature branch by design)
Maestro (works on a feature branch by design)
the one platform: Backstage catalog, the router, the standards page
the sops directory vault, the estate secrets standard
the survival lab and its DNS shim
the guard scaffolds every repo inherits
the deployed prospector checkout and its offsite drill

the estate's requirements ledger and agent-certification onboarding; it has a github remote and 0 commits off-remote, but nothing declared it, so no escrow rule reached it and its R2 copy sat at 472f783 while the disk moved to 7ca27f9

secrets.why: the credentials every estate job reads; the names are kept, the values never are

skip_names.comment: Not the estate's to keep: other vendors' jobs, and definitions deliberately parked.

always_dirty.comment: Append-only logs every session writes, and files a running service rewrites at boot. Flagging these forever would make the instrument cry wolf, which is LAW 28's failure, not LAW 24's.

escrow.comment: A repo pushed only to GitHub is one account suspension from gone. estate_bundle_push.sh writes a verified bundle offsite; this is the receipt it must produce.
